title: Battlebox Surge Playbook — shortstack
content:
Purpose: compact, action-first playbook for SEs + Ops to execute a rapid ‘surge recovery’ when live pilot traffic or demo load spikes threaten SLAs

Context + intent:
- This is a short, portable battlebox intended to be read in 3–5 minutes before a sync or during a rapid incident.
- Focus: restore predictable latency/cost behavior without full infra escalations. Keep the customer pilot alive.
- Audience: Sales Engineers, Field Ops, Customer Engineering, on-call SEs.

When to pull this out (triggers):
- Observed 95th percentile token latency > target SLA for > 3m
- Token/spike cost unexpectedly exceeds pilot budget threshold (alert: pilot-cost > 1.5x forecast)
- Model-level errors (OOMs, NVLINK faults) causing retries or timeouts
- Pilot is public-facing (demo/press) and latency risk must be minimized immediately

Three quick surge scenarios (ranked by severity):
1) Cold-start spike (short-lived, high concurrency)
   - Symptoms: sudden burst after marketing email / demo wave; KV cache misses; per-request overhead dominates
   - Immediate actions (0–5m):
     * Switch route to lower-latency model variant (policy: route -> model-variant-a-lite) — SE action via Console route toggle.
     * Enable prefix caching for expected prompts (if available) — add 1–2 tokens prefix prewarm.
     * If hosted plan, enable short-lived burst capacity (ops: enable ×2 burst)
   - Secondary (5–20m):
     * Scale dedicated pool workers temporarily (if Customer on Dedicated) or bump concurrency cap.
     * Add a short note to customer: “seeing a sudden demo wave; temporarily routing to a faster variant to keep UX snappy.”

2) Sustained high-throughput (minutes→hours)
   - Symptoms: throughput steady above allocated capacity, costs rising, tail latencies increasing
   - Immediate actions (0–10m):
     * Throttle non-critical routes via rate-limit tags (e.g., background-batch, metrics-scrape).
     * Enable autoretry backoff on client SDK (ask dev to flip feature flag).
     * Apply token-budget cap for demo tokens per-minute.
   - Secondary (10–60m):
     * Propose a short reserved bump (ops + sales) — 24–72 hour elevated commit.
     * Adjust batching config to larger batch sizes if latency budget allows.

3) Degraded model/hardware (errors, OOM, retries)
   - Symptoms: OOMs, GPU errors, high error-rates, incomplete responses
   - Immediate actions (0–5m):
     * Route to a compatible quantized fallback model (model-fallback-q4) with identical prompt mapping.
     * Enable degraded-mode responses: short-form outputs with clear truncation indicator.
     * Open incident stub and notify customer-facing channel.
   - Secondary (5–30m):
     * Autoscale replacement nodes or shift traffic to a different region.
     * Reviewed logs and collect example request ids for engineering triage.

One-slide TL;DR for an SE (copyable):
- "If latency spike: route to faster variant + enable prefix cache; if sustained spike: throttle non-critical routes + request temporary reserved bump; if errors: failover to quantized fallback and notify ops."

Technical fallback matrix (quick cheat):
- Latency vs quality tradeoffs:
  * Lower-latency variant = smaller transformer layers / shorter context / fp16 or q4_0 — expect slight quality shift for long-form completions.
  * Quantized fallback = cost down, errors down, possible hallucination risk on edge prompts.
- When to prefer console toggles vs infra scaling:
  * Console toggle (fastest): use when user experience must be preserved immediately.
  * Infra scaling (cost + time): use when expected impact > 30 minutes and revenue/hard SLA at risk.

Demo script — quick rescues (for SE to run live):
- Preflight (1m):
  1) Open Console → Routes → check active model variant.
  2) Open Telemetry → 95th latency, error rate, and recent request IDs.
- Live (actions):
  1) Toggle Route -> model-variant-a-lite.
  2) Turn on prefix cache for the demo prompt (copy common system prompt into cache).
  3) Post a short test request from Console to validate responses in < target latency.
- Post (note to customer):
  "We routed to a faster model and cached the common prompt to keep the demo snappy. We'll restore normal routing after traffic subsides — ETA 2–6 hours."

Suggested metrics to cite in customer notes (quick numbers to include):
- Baseline 95p latency (pre-surge): 120–250 ms per token (hosted small model)
- Surge fast fallback 95p: 70–160 ms per token (lite variant)
- Typical cost delta (per token): fallback → −25–45% depending on model family
- Recovery window estimate: toggles take ~30–90s to propagate across region

Quick objection scripts (customer-facing):
- If customer: "Won't quality degrade?" → "Short-term trade. We only route critical demo traffic to the faster variant; we keep the same prompt structure and will validate outputs. Longer-run analysis will guide next steps."
- If customer: "Will my data be routed elsewhere?" → "We use compatible model variants in-region and maintain data isolation policies; we only change model config, not data routing."

Common pitfalls and mitigation notes:
- Pitfall: toggling multiple routes at once -> config churn and inconsistent tracing.
  * Mitigation: change one route at a time and confirm with a smoke request.
- Pitfall: flipping to quantized fallback without prompt-normalization -> hallucinations.
  * Mitigation: shorten prompt, remove low-signal context, validate with known test prompts.

Open questions / items to iterate:
- Define a one-click Console macro for the 3-step rescue (toggle variant, enable cache, run smoke test). Owner: Product Console team — @Samir Nadeem (GH: console/macro-idea).
- SLA language to add to pilot contracts for temporary reserved bumps (legal + sales ops). Owner: Maya Lopez.
- Small after-action template to send customers post-surge (ops comms draft). Owner: Avery Chen.

Immediate next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Draft Console macro spec — Samir — due 2026-03-01
- [ ] Add short rescue flashcard to SE playbook — Maya — due 2026-02-28
- [ ] Create 3 smoke-test prompts and add to repo/demo-scripts — Evan — due 2026-02-21

Notes to self (raw, keep):
- Keep this doc intentionally short. SEs prefer a 30–60s skim then steps.
- We should capture two real pilot incidents and anonymized request ids for quick forensic examples.

Slack threads / links to mention in handoffs:
- #go-to-market-ops (surge notifications)
- #se-oncall (notify when executing toggles)

End of shortstack playbook — copy into SE cheat sheet or convert to 1-slide pocket.
